newsitem.title: USA: AT&T encouraged by new long distance plan.
newsitem.headline: AT&T encouraged by new long distance plan.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Thursday said its new single rate consumer and small business long distance marketing plan was showing early promise.
"While One Rate has only been in the market a few weeks we are pleased with the level of customer interest so far," chief financial officer Richard Miller told a conference call.
"The simplicity of the plan is resulting in a higher (deal) close rate for our sales representatives," he said.
The 15-cents per minute rate was introduced in September to fight off heavy competition in the long distance market.

Operating income in the consumer long distance segment was hit by higher spending to fight for customers in a highly competitive market. Overall selling general and administration expenses rose 21.6 percent from a year ago.
"This rise was driven by higher marketing costs particularly in the consumer segment," Miller said.
NCR Corp turned a $29 million operating profit in the quarter compared with a $196 million loss a year earlier.
"NCR is well on its way to becoming a profitable business," Miller said.

AT&T said total long distance calling volumes -- including the buoyant business market -- increased 5.1 percent from a year ago, and 2.6 percent from the second quarter, but revenues increased only 2.2 percent from the year-ago quarter.
Consumer market revenues were up only slightly from a year ago, while the business market grew more rapidly, he said.
"Volumes reflected double digit growth led by toll-free, 800 and 888 services," Miller said. He added that customised business services for large clients had been very succesful.
The operating margin in communications services as a whole slipped to 17.2 percent from 19.0 percent a year earlier.
Financial services revenues made an operating loss of $35 million from a $47 million profit a year ago.
Revenues fell 32 percent in the quarter from a year ago, mainly because of securitization of receivables at Universal Card, but also reflecting heightened competition.
The continued decline in portfolio performance and an increased risk profile of customers were to blame, AT&T said.
AT&T Financial Services president David Hunt resigned in September. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712
